v01.titulo: Airplane Window Hole: Why It's There On Purpose
v01.descripcion:
Every airplane window has a tiny hole in the middle pane. It keeps cabin pressure on the outer pane, so the middle one stays a fresh backup, and it lets moisture out so the window doesn't fog.

Sources: Mental Floss, Why do airplane windows have tiny holes? (mentalfloss.com) · AFAR, Why airplane windows have tiny holes (afar.com) · Cabin pressurization, Wikipedia.

v02.titulo: Padlock Hole: The Real Reason It's on the Bottom
v02.descripcion:
That tiny hole under a padlock is not a keyhole. It mainly drains rain that gets in through the keyhole, so the lock rusts less and doesn't freeze shut. Some lock makers also suggest lubricating through it.

Sources: House Digest, What is the tiny hole on the bottom of a padlock for? (housedigest.com) · Monroe Engineering, Why padlocks have a small hole on the bottom (monroeengineering.com).

v03.titulo: Fuel Gauge Arrow: The Real Story Behind It
v03.descripcion:
The little triangle next to your fuel gauge points to the side of your gas cap. Ford designer Jim Moylan proposed it in a 1986 memo after a rainy trip to the pump, and it first appeared on 1989 Ford models.

Sources: Motor1, What that little arrow next to the fuel gauge actually means (motor1.com) · The Drive, The Moylan Arrow is one of Ford's best contributions to car design (thedrive.com).

v04.titulo: F and J Bumps: The Real Reason They Exist
v04.descripcion:
The small bumps on F and J mark the home row, so your index fingers can find their place by touch and you can type without looking. The number pad has the same trick on the 5 key.

Sources: Computer Hope, Why are there bumps on the F and J keyboard keys? (computerhope.com) · Mental Floss, The reason for bumps on computer keys (mentalfloss.com).
